title: Cowboy Hat Stewardship IRSC - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
description: This Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government will not reimburse accompanying costs. Any answers or attachments provided are based upon the best information available at the time of the site visit and are subject to change. 1. Background & Purpose USDA Forest Service seeks capability statements from qualified vendors able to conduct forest thinning and vegetation treatments in areas burned by the Caldor Fire. The goals of the project are to reduce hazardous fuels and create conditions appropriate for reestablishing forested landscapes. Stewardship Authority shall be utilized to award an Integrated Resource Service Contract. In accordance with the approved NEPA decision, Cut-to-Length harvesting is the required logging mechanism. CTL typically consists of a harvester cutting and processing trees at the stump and a forwarder transporting the material to a designated landing location over a slash mat. The purpose of this SS/RFI is to gather information on vendor capabilities, invite prospective vendors to an organized site visit on 11/3/2026 before snow limits access, and provide draft documents to so that vendors can assess whether the opportunity is one to follow and potentially quote. 2. Anticipated Scope of Work The project objectives shall be met by performing the following service work. Cut, process, and forward to landings or pile included biomass in 3 units across 205 acres. Within these units, cut standing dead conifer trees and forward to landings or pile. Treat fuels by mechanically masticating existing dead and down material, project-generated slash and brush. Remove slash and large dead and down to landings when necessary to meet the fuels treatment specification. Remove biomass and cull logs from landings to off-Forest disposal sites. Construct temporary road to facilitate thinning treatment and decommission the roads prior to demobilization. Perform road maintenance and erosion control on roads used for biomass removal or otherwise damaged by Contractor�s operations. Perform hand thinning and piling if awarded. 3. Place of Performance The project is located on the Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit in portions of Township 11N Range 18E Section 5, and Township 12N Range 18E Sections 32 and 33; Mount Diablo Meridian, approximately 0.5 miles southeast of the intersection of California Highway 89 and US Highway 50. 4. Period of Performance Anticipated start date: Early Summer 2027. Performance deadline: 9/15/2027. This deadline is linked to grant funding expiration. 5. Site Visit An organized site visit will occur on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. local time. Interested parties will meet in South Lake Tahoe, CA at the east end of Oneidas Street at the Forest Service Gate: 38�51'53.0"N 119�59'40.7"W. This location is south of Lake Tahoe Airport off of Pioneer Trail Road. Interested parties should email Karen Ruklic at karen.ruklic@usda.gov by 1:00 p.m. PT on November 2, 2026, if they plan to attend. 6. Requested Capability Statement Content Company information (UEI, address, email, POC, business size and socio-economic status). Relevant experience focused on thinning via Cut-to-Length logging system and hazardous fuel reduction. Key personnel and crew qualifications. Equipment lists and mobilization capabilities. Past performance references. 7. Response Instructions & Due Date Any information submitted by vendors to this this SS/RFI is voluntary. Responses should be submitted electronically to Karen Ruklic at karen.ruklic@usda.gov. All responses are due no later than Monday, November 2, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. PT.

title: Troubleshooting, Calibration and as-needed Remedial Repair of Proof Test Machines
description: Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PHNSY & IMF) is a US Navy regional industrial center that maintains, overhauls and repairs various vessels of the US Navy. Its industrial operations provide the US naval forces with a wide range of services and resources located on the island of Oahu, Hawaii, with direct and indirect support to submarines, surface vessels and shore based activities in the Pacific. PHNSY & IMF seeks services to calibrate, provide preventative maintenance and as-needed remedial repairs of three (3) Government-owned Roberts Testing Proof Test Machines to ensure their accuracy, reliability, and safe operation. The Contractor shall provide all necessary labor, materials, and expertise to perform comprehensive calibration, preventative maintenance and as-needed remedial repair services on the Government-owned equipment specified in the Performance Work Statement (PWS) The tentative period of performance for this service: Base Period*: From 16 November 2026 to 15 November 2027 Option Periods*: Option Period 1: 16 November 2027 to 15 November 2028 Option Period 2: 16 November 2028 to 15 November 2029 Option Period 3: 16 November 2029 to 15 November 2030 Option Period 4: 16 November 2030 to 15 November 2031 6 month Option Period: 16 November 2031 to 15 May 2032 *(Performance period may be updated.) The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 541380, Testing Laboratories and Services; Size Standard $19,000,000.00. Product Service Code is L049, Technical representative services- maintenance and repair shop equipment. Please note the following: The solicitation number for this requirement is N32253-27-Q-0001 Quotes are due no later than 11/02/2026 at 11:00 a.m. HST. Quotes must be sent via email to both the primary and secondary points of contact. All firms or individuals responding must be registered with the System for Award Management(SAM) (https://www.sam.gov) by the award date. As part of the price quote package, the Offeror shall submit the completed SF 1449 with blocks 17a., 30a., 30b. and 30c. (SF 1449 page 1) and CLIN information (SF 1449 page�s 3-5) completed. Submission of a signed offer to the Government constitutes agreement and acceptance of the solicited terms and conditions. The Government may revise the solicitation at any time by means of an Amendment. It is an offeror�s responsibility to ensure it is accessing the Government Point of Entry (GPE) website, https://sam.gov/, to view potential amendments and procurement notifications for this solicitation. The proposal shall include: Technical Capability - Please submit a detailed technical quote (not to exceed 10 pages) that clearly demonstrates thorough knowledge and understanding of, and approach to completing the work in accordance with the PWS. The technical quote must contain sufficient details so that it may be evaluated in accordance with the PWS and comply with the period of performance set forth in the solicitation. Nonconformance will deem an Offeror ineligible. The technical quote must consist of a clear plan demonstrating how the offeror will Perform Calibration, Preventative Maintenance and as-needed Remedial Repair Services as required in the PWS. Certifications - Offerors must provide proof it meets the requirements set forth in NAVSEAINST 4734.1B, "Commercial calibration activities, including Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM), that calibrate NAVSEA TMDE will be certified or accredited by an accrediting body approved NAVSEA 04 to be in compliance with references (p), (r) and/or (s), and the scope of accreditation must cover the appropriate measurement parameters and ranges of the calibrations performed." The Contractor must, for the entire period of performance, maintain a certification or accreditation in compliance with NAVSEAINST 4734.1B. The Contractor's accreditation body must be approved by NAVSEA 04, and the scope of accreditation must encompass all measurement parameters and ranges for the NAVSEA Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE) calibrated under this contract. The Contractor shall make proof of current certification available for Government inspection upon request. Itemized Price Breakdown - Provide an itemized price breakdown of the quote that clearly and concisely describes and defines the Offeror's response to the requirements contained in the solicitation. Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC): DFARS clause 252.204-7021 and DFARS provision 252.204-7025 related to Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) requirements are included in the solicitation involving Federal Contract Information (FCI) or Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), on unclassified information systems, effective November 10, 2025. Offerors must possess a valid CMMC Level 1 (Self Assessment) certification at the time of award and for the duration of any resulting contract. The Government will verify the Offeror's CMMC Level 1 (Self-Assessment) certification at the time of award. Offerors failing to meet the requirements in DFARS clause 252.204-7021 and DFARS provision 252.204-7025 will be deemed ineligible for award. The Offeror shall provide, in the proposal, the CMMC unique identifier(s) (CMMC UIDs) issued by SPRS for each contractor information system that will process, store, or transmit FCI or CUI during performance of a contract, task order, or delivery order resulting from this solicitation. Offers must be received no later than the exact closing date and time specified in Block 8 of the SF 1449 (or as updated via subsequent amendments). Offerors are hereby advised that the size limit including attachments is 35 MB per email. Emails that exceed this size limit will not be received by the Government. It is the Offeror's sole responsibility to ensure their Offer is received by the Government POCs no later than the specified closing date and time. When necessary to comply with this size limit, the Offeror may deliver their Offer through multiple emails, with each email clearly marked in the Subject Line indicating its sequence order within the total number of emails being transmitted (for example, email 1 of 3). Offers received after the due date may not be considered unless the Contracting Officer determines that the delay was caused solely by the Government and accepting the Offer is in the best interest of the Government. Contract award will be in accordance to 52.212-2 as stated in the solicitation. All questions regarding solicitation N32253-25-Q-0001 shall be submitted in writing via email to the listed POCs. Questions are due 10/23/2026 03:00 PM HST.

F--Navajo Area - Abandoned Mines Response and Construction Services
description: Pre-Solicitation Notice Amendment for Navajo Area Abandoned Mines Response and Construction Services II (AMRCS II). This is a Request for Information (RFI) regarding the attached Draft Request for Proposal (DRFP). The DRFP is being released for COMMENT ONLY. This is not a synopsis proceeding the issuance of a solicitation. It is market research issued solely for information purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or any other solicitation. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA) is not seeking proposals at this time. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay any cost incurred in response to this notice. All costs associated with responding to this notice will solely be at the interested parties' expense. Any information provided by industry to the Government as a result of this notice is voluntary. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. It is recommended that interested parties monitor the FEDCONNECT website (https://www.fedconnect.net) for any information that may pertain to this notice. The information provided in this notice is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. The purpose of this RFI is to Request Comment on the DRFP for this requirement; which includes potential evaluation criteria for Navajo area- Abandoned Mines Response and Construction Services (AMRCS). To ensure the formal solicitation is executed in the most effective manner possible, we are posting the DRFP to offer an opportunity for industry to provide feedback. Your questions and input will be used to further refine, improve, or clarify these requirements. All Information and documentation posted under this notice are preliminary in nature and may be updated or amended prior to the release of the formal solicitation. NOTICE INFORMATION 1. SOLICITATION NUMBER: 68HE0926R0006 2. TITLE: Navajo Area- Abandoned Mines Response and Construction Services (AMRCS) 3. PRODUCT SERVICE CODE: F108- Hazardous Substance Removal, Cleanup, and Disposal Services 4. NAICS CODE: 562910- Environmental Remediation Services- Environmental Remediation Services a. Size Standard: 750 Employees 5. ANTICIPATED RFP RELEASE: Fall 2026 6. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE: Single award Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) 7. DESCRIPTION a. Background: Under the authority of Section 104 of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) or Super fund of 1980, as amended by the Superfund Amendments and Reauthorization Act (SARA); Subtitle I of the Resource Conservation and Recover y Act (RCRA) and pursuant to the National Oil and Hazardous Substances Pollution Contingency Plan (NCP) (40 CFR Part 300); and in accordance with any reauthorizations or amendment s to any of the above named statutes and new response legislation, the EPA has been delegated the responsibility to undertake response actions with respect to the release or threat of release of hazardous substances, or pollutants and contaminants, that pose an actual or potential threat to human health or welfare, or to the environment. b. Navajo Area Uranium Mines (USEPA Region 9) The Navajo Nation encompasses more than 27,000 square miles, spread amongst the Four Corners Region of the USA (Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, and Arizona). The unique geology of the region makes the Navajo Nation rich in uranium, a radioactive ore in high demand after the development of atomic power and weapons at the close of World War II in the 1940s. Approximately four million tons of uranium ore were extracted during mining operations within the Navajo Nation from 1944 to 1986. Many Navajo people worked the mines, often living and raising families in close proximity to the mines and mills. Uranium mining and milling activities no longer occur on Navajo lands, but the legacy of these activities remains, including more than 500 abandoned uranium mine claims with thousands of mine features such as pits, trenches, holes, etc., and homes and drinking water sources with elevated levels of uranium, radium and other radionuclides. Uranium and other elements (selenium, arsenic, etc.) associated with mine and mill sites also occur naturally at elevated levels in rock, soil, surface water, and groundwater across the Navajo Nation and the broader Four Corners region. USEPA maintains a strong partnership with the Navajo Nation and, since 1994, the USEPA Superfund Program has provided technical assistance and funding to assess potentially contaminated sites and develop a response. In August 2007, the USEPA Superfund Program compiled a Comprehensive Database and Atlas of all known uranium mines on the Navajo Nation. In October 2007, at the request of the U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, EPA, along with the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA), the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), the Department of Energy (DOE), and the Indian Health Service (IHS) developed a coordinated https://www.epa.gov/navajo-nation-uranium-cleanup to address uranium contamination in consultation with Navajo Nation EPA. d. Region 9 The primary hazardous substance on all the sites referenced in the requirement�s Statement of Work (SOW) is radiological mine and mine related waste; therefore, a significant knowledge base of radiological material handling, environmental data interpretation, and data collection will be required to perform the activities within this SOW. The terrain to access site locations is rough, water is scarce, and the weather is often extreme in most areas. The trails and/or roads to the sites are not improved or maintained. To reach the site locations, 4-wheel drive vehicles (capable of drives over rough dirt/rocky roads) and/or hiking long distances is required. Roads can become impassable in wet weather, and conditions can change quickly. In summer, the conditions are hot and dry; in winter, elevations make them subject to severe cold and high winds. Due to the quick changes in the weather, be aware of the danger of flash floods. While this danger is greatest during the summer monsoon season (July through September), flash floods can occur at any time of the year. e. Purpose and Objectives: The purpose of the Navajo Area Abandoned Mines Response and Construction Services (AMRCS) contract is to provide cleanup, response, and construction services to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), primarily at former uranium mining-related sites on or within the Navajo Nation (within EPA Region 9 in Arizona and New Mexico). 7. DESCRIPTION OF INFORMATION REQUESTED: The USEPA is seeking comments on the attached DRFP. The Government will consider all comments, questions, and issues raised by all prospective offerors in formulating requirements for any resultant solicitation document. The information contained here reflects the Government's anticipated requirements as of the date on this posting. The purpose of this notice is to solicit comments regarding a possible acquisition. The issuance of this notice is designed to gather as much information as possible to ensure that the Government's requirements are clear and concise; and possibly improve the requirements based on industry best practices and lessons learned, which may be stated in a future solicitation. SUBMITTAL INFORMATION A cover page and an executive summary may be included in the response, but is not required. All interested parties may respond. At a minimum, responses should include the following: a. Business name, SAM Unique Entity ID, business address, size and type of business (e.g., Large Business, Small Business, 8(a), HubZone, Woman Owned Small Business etc.) pursuant to the applicable NAICS code, and the name, telephone number, mailing address, and email address of a point of contact having authority and knowledge to discuss responses with Government representatives.

title: 35HAV26 - Kjøp av kabelhåndteringssystem (CMS) til Kneppeskjær
description: Oslo Havn KF (HAV) har fått tilsagn støtte fra Enova til et landstrømanlegg på Kneppeskjær. Anlegget må oppfylle kravene i tildelingsbrevet fra Enova. Dette omfatter blant annet kravene i NEK IEC PAS 80005-3. Leverandør av landstrømanlegget og uttaksskap er allerede tildelt, og arbeidet på kaien er påbegynt. Landstrømanlegget skal forsyne skip på Kneppeskjær kai på Sjursøya. Kneppeskjær kai er delt i to deler: øst og vest. Det skal være tre uttaksskap og være dimensjonert for en effekt på 1600 kVA ved 690 V og 50 Hz. Denne anskaffelsen omfatter kjøp av tre kabelhåndteringssystemer (CMS, Cable Management System) som skal brukes til å koble kablene mellom uttaksskap/grensesnittskap og skipene. Dette inkluderer 1 stk. kabeltårn for CCS-skip og 2. stk mobile kabelhåndteringssystem. Betegnelsen CMS vil brukes som en fellesbetegnelse for de tre kabelhåndteringssystemene. Anskaffelsen omfatter også en treårig serviceavtale for kabeltårnet og en treårig serviceavtale for de mobile kabelhåndteringssystemene. I tillegg inkluderer anskaffelsen følgende opsjoner: Opsjon 1: 2 stk. mobile kabelhåndteringssystemer Opsjon 2: Tilkoblinger etter prøvedrift Opsjon 3: Reserveplugger Opsjon 4: Blindkontakter Opsjon 5: Garanti Opsjon 6: Serviceavtale Leverandøren er anvarlig for koordinering med leverandøren av landstrømanlegget (Powercon). Oppdragsgiver ønsker de mobile kabelhåndteringssysteme og kabeltårnet skal leveres så snart som mulig, senest innen 12 måneder etter kontraktinngåelse. Leverandøren skal som del av sitt tilbud angi leveringstid for kabeltårn og de mobile kabelhåndteringsystemene.

buyer: Oslo kommune v/ Oslo Havn KF
title: Norway – Electricity distribution and control apparatus – 35HAV26 - Procurement of a cable management system (CMS) for Kneppeskjær
description: The Port of Oslo (HAV) has received support from Enova for an on-shore power plant at Kneppeskjær. The facility must meet the requirements in the award letter from Enova. This includes i.a. the requirements in NEK IEC PAS 80005-3. The supplier of the land power system and power cabinets has already been awarded, and work on the quay has begun. The land power plant shall supply the ship at Kneppeskjær quay on Sjursøya. The kneppeskjær quay is divided into two parts: east and west. There shall be three extraction cabinets and dimensioned for an output of 1600 kVA at 690 V and 50 Hz. This procurement is for the procurement of three cable management systems (CMS, Cable Management System) that shall be used to connect the cables between the socket cupboards/interface cabinets and the ships. This includes 1 cable tower for CCS ships and 2 mobile cable handling systems. The term CMS will be used as a generic term for the three cable handling systems. The procurement also includes a three year service agreement for the cable tower and a three year service contract for the mobile cable handling systems. In addition the procurement includes the following options: Option 1: 2 mobile cable management systems. Option 2: Connections after trial operation Option 3: Spare plugs Option 4: Blind contacts Option 5: Guarantee Option 6: Service contract The tenderer is required to be coordinated with the supplier of the land power system (Powercon). The contracting authority would like the mobile cable management systems and the cable tower shall be delivered as soon as possible, at the latest within 12 months after the contract has been signed. Tenderers shall, as part of their tender, state the delivery time for cable towers and the mobile cable management systems.

title: Request for Information - Energetics Center of Excellence
description: Request for Information - Energetics Center of Excellence 1.0 Purpose Army Contracting Command�Rock Island, on behalf of Portfolio Acquisition Executive Agile Sustainment & Ammunition and Project Lead Joint Services, is requesting information from industry regarding transformative projects, programs, capabilities, and concepts that would strengthen the Department of War (DoW) energetics ecosystem and resiliency within the Defense Industrial Base (DIB). This Request for Information (RFI) is intended to inform potential use of funding for energetics resilience at Blue Grass Army Depot (BGAD) in Richmond, Kentucky. The Government is intentionally non-prescriptive regarding detailed technical or product requirement through this RFI. Rather, the Government seeks industry input on both defense and commercially executable solutions that address energetic-resiliency challenges through a potential Private-Public Partnership (P3). This request for information is for market research purposes only and is not a formal contract offer. Your response cannot be accepted to form a binding contract, and the Army is not at this time seeking proposals. 2.0 Problem Statement The DoW energetics enterprise faces increasing demand while portions of the supporting industrial base remain constrained by limited domestic capacity, aging infrastructure, legacy manufacturing processes, long qualification timelines, and fragile or concentrated supply chains. These constraints pose a risk to warfighter readiness, ability to rapidly scale during periods of additional demand, and constrain the ability to field next generation munitions. 3.0 Scope and Desired Solutions Industry may propose concepts across the full energetics spectrum or energetics value chain that include discrete projects, multiple coordinated but independently executable project modules, or a master-campus concept involving complementary capabilities. The Government seeks practical, scalable, and commercially sustainable solutions during future periods of low to no government orders that may include, but are not limited to: Onshoring: Establishing domestic production capacity for energetics products, inputs, components, precursors, or processing capabilities currently produced OCONUS. Supply-Chain Resilience: Reducing foreign, sole-source, or other critical supply-chain dependencies; increasing domestic redundancy; and eliminating or mitigating single-point production failures. Flexible Production Capacity: Modernizing, supplementing, or replacing legacy manufacturing and processing methods through automation, digital process control, flexible manufacturing (modular, reconfigurable, multi-product production lines that can support multiple products, formulations, customers, or demand scenarios), advanced quality assurance, continuous or semi-continuous processing, or similar approaches to create the flexibility needed to quickly scale up for surge requirements. Next-Generation Formulation Transition: Establish medium-scale production and scale-up capability to accelerate transition of next-generation formulations from small scale lab to production-representative and full-rate manufacturing. Commercially Sustainable Operations: Establishing a dual-use, single/multi-tenant, or other commercial model capable of sustaining operations through peacetime by utilizing widely available commercial industry processes, manufacturing, and materials while retaining readiness to support defense surge requirements. 4.0 Threshold Criteria and Limitations Respondents have broad latitude regarding the solution proposed. However, each concept should meet the following threshold criteria and limitations. 4.1 Geographic Location � BGAD, Richmond, Kentucky All proposed physical facilities, pilot lines, processing units, laboratories, capital improvements, and associated support infrastructure must be located at BGAD. 4.2 DIB Synergy and Alignment Proposed capabilities must be new, unique, and complete or provide complementary, supplementary, or redundant/resilient production capabilities within the existing Contractor-Owned, Contractor-Operated (COCO), Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO), and Government-Owned, Government-Operated (GOGO) Army network. 4.3 Commercial Viability and No Planned Recurring Government Support The Government seeks concepts that do not rely on planned recurring U.S. Government funding for steady-state facility operations, maintenance, staffing, overhead, or routine upkeep after establishment. The Government would be interested in respondent, commercial, or third-party co-investment, where applicable. 4.4 Schedule The Government is seeking a Period of Performance (PoP) of 48 months or less to achieve full project transition and commissioning. The Army is focused on rapid capability acceleration, earlier completion timelines are highly encouraged. 5.0 Submission Requirements Responses are limited to a maximum of 10 pages, which must detail the following: Project description and expected warfighter / DIB impact; Technical approach, modernization method, and next-generation formulation transition plan; Commercial products or services utilization to keep the facility viable during period of low to no USG orders; Onshoring, supply-chain resilience, and foreign-dependency reduction benefits; Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) that includes the cost for design, construction, and commissioning, rationale for dual-use sustainable business model, and optional self/co-investment; Execution milestones to the complete path within 48 months or less. 6.0 Point of Contact and Submission Deadline Industry is requested to submit responses to this RFI no later than 4:00pm central 02 November 2026. Responses and questions regarding this RFI shall be submitted to: Contracting Officer: SFC Pramod Khanal at pramod.khanal.mil@army.mil Contract Specialist: Lindsey Arguello at lindsey.j.arguello.civ@army.mil 7.0 Industry Day The Government plans to have further conversation with industry and shape the Energetics Center of Excellence requirement at the GOCO Industry Day in November 2026 referenced here: https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/73cb195b4756453494768ade061e21aa/view. Industry Day details and registration information will be provided in a subsequent update to the GOCO Industry Day announcement. Registration is not required at this time. Disclaimer The Government does not intend to reimburse any contractor for any information or administrative costs associated with responding to this notification. Participation in this survey is strictly voluntary. Any information stated above is subject to change. Respondents are responsible for appropriately marking any proprietary information. This is a Sources Sought notice for market research purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a commitment to issue an RFP in the future.

Questions seeking input on potential collaboration with DOE-EM on Critical Minerals and Materials Inventory Specific Questions: Note: The terms recovery, reuse, repurposing, and reprocessing are viewed as interchangeable in this context but DOE will use the term reuse throughout for consistency. What specific needs or demands does your organization have for rare earth metals, critical minerals, or materials that could be met by the DOE inventory? Describe your organization's technical capabilities and experience in handling, processing, mining, or extracting rare earth metals, critical minerals, or materials. Please detail your proposed plan's material requirements, specifying the minimum viable quantity, the optimal quantity for maximizing impact, and how the plan's scalability accommodates varying amounts from the available inventory. What potential applications, domestic sectors, or market demand does your organization foresee for your proposed reuse? Describe how your proposed reuse of inventory material(s) and any resulting products will primarily benefit U.S. domestic needs and contribute to the resilience of the U.S. energy and manufacturing supply chain. What are your proposed plans for the management and disposal of any waste streams or byproducts generated from your processing or repurposing activities involving the inventory materials? All other terms and conditions remain unchanged. _______________________________________________________________________ The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of YT-811. The YT-811 characteristics are Length: 90 FT, Width: 38FT 5IN, Age: 4 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 16 FT, Full Displacement: 494 L Tons and Light Load: 438 L Tons. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of YT-811 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. The Government will transport the vessel to the Contractors repair facility. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Replace zinc anodes. Blast and preserve underwater hull and freeboard, bulwarks, and handrails. Blast and preserve main deck, 1st deck, and 2nd deck non-skid, FME all polished stainless steel surfaces. Perform hull and freeboard Ultrasonic Test (UT) inspections. Perform hull and freeboard, main deck, 1st deck, and 2nd deck Visual Inspections (VT). Repair hull and winch valves. Repair deckhouse expansion joint. Test and preserve CHT, ballast, potable water, fuel oil, waste oil and day tanks. Accomplish Mast Lighting and Deckhouse Lighting Repairs. Replace all placards and labels on main, 1st and 2nd decks. Replace deck winch, mast, and brow systems hydraulic hoses. Accomplish winch control piping modification (YT-0104D). Overhaul Mast hydraulic ram, replace pins and bushings. Undock the vessel. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the SUPERVISOR. Upon completion of all work the Government will take custody of the vessel. Specific details of all work items and tasks required by this Statement of Work described in this Scope Overview are included in section 3.0 of this Statement of Work. The YT-811 will be ready for pick up on or after 2 March 2027. Refer to page 1 Request for Quote (RFQ) of the Solicitation regarding desired and required delivery information. description: DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY Expression of Interest�DOE�s Office of Environmental Management (DOE-EM) Critical Minerals and Materials Inventory. AGENCY: Office of Environmental Management, Department of Energy. ACTION: Expression of Interest (EOI). SUMMARY: The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Environmental Management (EM) publishes the following questions regarding potential collaboration with interested parties for the reuse of its critical and rare earth minerals and materials. The goal is to ensure surplus critical minerals and materials within the DOE inventory are repurposed to bolster and diversify the U.S. supply chain. This will support domestic scientific, manufacturing, and energy needs. A list of materials and minerals in DOE�s inventory is supplied as an attachment. Respondents should note that industry partners would be responsible for the subsequent extraction or reprocessing of the material. THIS IS AN EXPRESSION OF INTEREST ONLY. THIS NOTICE DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A NOTICE OF FUNDING OPPORTUNITY (NOFO). A NOFO DOES NOT EXIST AT THIS TIME. DOE will not provide funding or compensation for any information submitted in response to this EOI. This EOI is not seeking or accepting applications, and a response to this EOI will not be viewed as a binding commitment to develop or pursue the ideas discussed. No material submitted for review will be returned. DATES: Responses to the EOI must be received no later than November 2, 2026. A virtual Industry Day will be held on September 30, 2026. For questions and a link to attend, please email Rob Seifert, robert.seifert@em.doe.gov. ADDRESSES: Interested parties are to submit comments electronically to robert.seifert@em.doe.gov with the subject line �EM Critical Minerals Inventory� no later than November 2, 2026. All responses must be submitted as a Microsoft Word document (.doc/.docx) of no more than five (5) pages in length, with black, Times New Roman, 12-point font, and 1-inch margins as an attachment to an email. The document cannot exceed 2MB in size. Only electronic responses to the above email address will be accepted. DOE will not consider responses submitted by any other means. Note: If clicking on the above link gives you an error message, you must CUT AND PASTE the URL into your browser to reach the web page. FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Rob Seifert, (301)-250-5239, robert.seifert@em.doe.gov. Questions seeking input on potential collaboration with DOE-EM on Critical Minerals and Materials Inventory Specific Questions: Note: The terms recovery, reuse, repurposing, and reprocessing are viewed as interchangeable in this context but DOE will use the term reuse throughout for consistency. What specific needs or demands does your organization have for rare earth metals, critical minerals, or materials that could be met by the DOE inventory? Describe your organization's technical capabilities and experience in handling, processing, mining, or extracting rare earth metals, critical minerals, or materials. Please detail your proposed plan's material requirements, specifying the minimum viable quantity, the optimal quantity for maximizing impact, and how the plan's scalability accommodates varying amounts from the available inventory. What potential applications, domestic sectors, or market demand does your organization foresee for your proposed reuse? Describe how your proposed reuse of inventory material(s) and any resulting products will primarily benefit U.S. domestic needs and contribute to the resilience of the U.S. energy and manufacturing supply chain. How would your organization propose collaborating with DOE-EM to facilitate the reuse of the inventory materials? Outline any significant technical, logistical or regulatory challenges anticipated in the reuse of material(s) from the DOE inventory and how these would be addressed or contingency plans. What are your proposed plans for the management and disposal of any waste streams or byproducts generated from your processing or repurposing activities involving the inventory materials? Would your organization be interested in exploring the possibility of leasing land or developing a facility on a site for material processing, repurposing, or related activities? If so, please provide details on your potential interest and any requirements or considerations for such an undertaking. title: Request for Information - Energetics Center of Excellence
description: Request for Information - Energetics Center of Excellence 1.0 Purpose Army Contracting Command�Rock Island, on behalf of Portfolio Acquisition Executive Agile Sustainment & Ammunition and Project Lead Joint Services, is requesting information from industry regarding transformative projects, programs, capabilities, and concepts that would strengthen the Department of War (DoW) energetics ecosystem and resiliency within the Defense Industrial Base (DIB). This Request for Information (RFI) is intended to inform potential use of funding for energetics resilience at Blue Grass Army Depot (BGAD) in Richmond, Kentucky. The Government is intentionally non-prescriptive regarding detailed technical or product requirement through this RFI. Rather, the Government seeks industry input on both defense and commercially executable solutions that address energetic-resiliency challenges through a potential Private-Public Partnership (P3). This request for information is for market research purposes only and is not a formal contract offer. Your response cannot be accepted to form a binding contract, and the Army is not at this time seeking proposals. 2.0 Problem Statement The DoW energetics enterprise faces increasing demand while portions of the supporting industrial base remain constrained by limited domestic capacity, aging infrastructure, legacy manufacturing processes, long qualification timelines, and fragile or concentrated supply chains. These constraints pose a risk to warfighter readiness, ability to rapidly scale during periods of additional demand, and constrain the ability to field next generation munitions. 3.0 Scope and Desired Solutions Industry may propose concepts across the full energetics spectrum or energetics value chain that include discrete projects, multiple coordinated but independently executable project modules, or a master-campus concept involving complementary capabilities. The Government seeks practical, scalable, and commercially sustainable solutions during future periods of low to no government orders that may include, but are not limited to: Onshoring: Establishing domestic production capacity for energetics products, inputs, components, precursors, or processing capabilities currently produced OCONUS. Supply-Chain Resilience: Reducing foreign, sole-source, or other critical supply-chain dependencies; increasing domestic redundancy; and eliminating or mitigating single-point production failures. Flexible Production Capacity: Modernizing, supplementing, or replacing legacy manufacturing and processing methods through automation, digital process control, flexible manufacturing (modular, reconfigurable, multi-product production lines that can support multiple products, formulations, customers, or demand scenarios), advanced quality assurance, continuous or semi-continuous processing, or similar approaches to create the flexibility needed to quickly scale up for surge requirements. Next-Generation Formulation Transition: Establish medium-scale production and scale-up capability to accelerate transition of next-generation formulations from small scale lab to production-representative and full-rate manufacturing. Commercially Sustainable Operations: Establishing a dual-use, single/multi-tenant, or other commercial model capable of sustaining operations through peacetime by utilizing widely available commercial industry processes, manufacturing, and materials while retaining readiness to support defense surge requirements. 4.0 Threshold Criteria and Limitations Respondents have broad latitude regarding the solution proposed. However, each concept should meet the following threshold criteria and limitations. 4.1 Geographic Location � BGAD, Richmond, Kentucky All proposed physical facilities, pilot lines, processing units, laboratories, capital improvements, and associated support infrastructure must be located at BGAD. 4.2 DIB Synergy and Alignment Proposed capabilities must be new, unique, and complete or provide complementary, supplementary, or redundant/resilient production capabilities within the existing Contractor-Owned, Contractor-Operated (COCO), Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO), and Government-Owned, Government-Operated (GOGO) Army network. 4.3 Commercial Viability and No Planned Recurring Government Support The Government seeks concepts that do not rely on planned recurring U.S. Government funding for steady-state facility operations, maintenance, staffing, overhead, or routine upkeep after establishment. The Government would be interested in respondent, commercial, or third-party co-investment, where applicable. 4.4 Schedule The Government is seeking a Period of Performance (PoP) of 48 months or less to achieve full project transition and commissioning. The Army is focused on rapid capability acceleration, earlier completion timelines are highly encouraged. 5.0 Submission Requirements Responses are limited to a maximum of 10 pages, which must detail the following: Project description and expected warfighter / DIB impact; Technical approach, modernization method, and next-generation formulation transition plan; Commercial products or services utilization to keep the facility viable during period of low to no USG orders; Onshoring, supply-chain resilience, and foreign-dependency reduction benefits; Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) that includes the cost for design, construction, and commissioning, rationale for dual-use sustainable business model, and optional self/co-investment; Execution milestones to the complete path within 48 months or less. 6.0 Point of Contact and Submission Deadline Industry is requested to submit responses to this RFI no later than 4:00pm central 02 November 2026. Responses and questions regarding this RFI shall be submitted to: Contracting Officer: SFC Pramod Khanal at pramod.khanal.mil@army.mil Contract Specialist: Lindsey Arguello at lindsey.j.arguello.civ@army.mil 7.0 Industry Day The Government plans to have further conversation with industry and shape the Energetics Center of Excellence requirement at the GOCO Industry Day in November 2026 referenced here: https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/73cb195b4756453494768ade061e21aa/view. Industry Day details and registration information will be provided in a subsequent update to the GOCO Industry Day announcement. Registration is not required at this time. Disclaimer The Government does not intend to reimburse any contractor for any information or administrative costs associated with responding to this notification. Participation in this survey is strictly voluntary. Any information stated above is subject to change. Respondents are responsible for appropriately marking any proprietary information. This is a Sources Sought notice for market research purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a commitment to issue an RFP in the future.

title: Maintenance, Repair and Preservation of YT-811
description: The Solicitation number has been updated from N4523A26Q1012 to N4523A27Q0002. Total Small Business Set-aside has been updated on SAM to reflect the Solcitation. PURPOSE: The purpose of this amendment is to update the following: Attachment 1 Statement of Work Rev 1, Attachment 2 Price Worksheet Rev 1, Attachment 6 Drawings and References Rev 1, and add RFC Questions/Answers sheet. The following clauses were added: 252.217-7006, 252.217-7012, 252.217-7014, and 252.217-7016. SCHEDULE: The proposal due date and time has been extended to 2:00PM PST, 02 November 2026. TERMS: Added clause 252.217-7006, 252.217-7012, 252.217-7014, and 252.217-7016. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged. _______________________________________________________________________ The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of YT-811. The YT-811 characteristics are Length: 90 FT, Width: 38FT 5IN, Age: 4 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 16 FT, Full Displacement: 494 L Tons and Light Load: 438 L Tons. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of YT-811 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. The Government will transport the vessel to the Contractors repair facility. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Replace zinc anodes. Blast and preserve underwater hull and freeboard, bulwarks, and handrails. Blast and preserve main deck, 1st deck, and 2nd deck non-skid, FME all polished stainless steel surfaces. Perform hull and freeboard Ultrasonic Test (UT) inspections. Perform hull and freeboard, main deck, 1st deck, and 2nd deck Visual Inspections (VT). Repair hull and winch valves. Repair deckhouse expansion joint. Test and preserve CHT, ballast, potable water, fuel oil, waste oil and day tanks. Accomplish Mast Lighting and Deckhouse Lighting Repairs. Replace all placards and labels on main, 1st and 2nd decks. Replace deck winch, mast, and brow systems hydraulic hoses. Accomplish winch control piping modification (YT-0104D). Overhaul Mast hydraulic ram, replace pins and bushings. Undock the vessel. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the SUPERVISOR. Upon completion of all work the Government will take custody of the vessel. Specific details of all work items and tasks required by this Statement of Work described in this Scope Overview are included in section 3.0 of this Statement of Work. The YT-811 will be ready for pick up on or after 2 March 2027. Refer to page 1 Request for Quote (RFQ) of the Solicitation regarding desired and required delivery information. This is full and open competition. All offerors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) to receive award of Government contracts. Offerors are advised also that SAM representations and certifications can be completed electronically via the System for Award Management website at https://www.sam.gov.

title: DOE Critical Mineral Resource Potential
description: September 30, 2026 DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY Expression of Interest�DOE�s Office of Environmental Management (DOE-EM) Critical Minerals and Materials Inventory. AGENCY: Office of Environmental Management, Department of Energy. ACTION: Expression of Interest (EOI). SUMMARY: The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Environmental Management (EM) publishes the following questions regarding potential collaboration with interested parties for the reuse of its critical and rare earth minerals and materials. The goal is to ensure surplus critical minerals and materials within the DOE inventory are repurposed to bolster and diversify the U.S. supply chain. This will support domestic scientific, manufacturing, and energy needs. A list of materials and minerals in DOE�s inventory is supplied as an attachment. Respondents should note that industry partners would be responsible for the subsequent extraction or reprocessing of the material. THIS IS AN EXPRESSION OF INTEREST ONLY. THIS NOTICE DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A NOTICE OF FUNDING OPPORTUNITY (NOFO). A NOFO DOES NOT EXIST AT THIS TIME. DOE will not provide funding or compensation for any information submitted in response to this EOI. This EOI is not seeking or accepting applications, and a response to this EOI will not be viewed as a binding commitment to develop or pursue the ideas discussed. No material submitted for review will be returned. DATES: Responses to the EOI must be received no later than November 2, 2026. A virtual Industry Day will be held on September 30, 2026. For questions and a link to attend, please email DOECriticalMinerals@doe.gov. ADDRESSES: Interested parties are to submit comments electronically to DOECriticalMinerals@doe.gov with the subject line �EM Critical Minerals Inventory� no later than November 2, 2026. All responses must be submitted as a Microsoft Word document (.doc/.docx) of no more than five (5) pages in length, with black, Times New Roman, 12-point font, and 1-inch margins as an attachment to an email. The document cannot exceed 2MB in size. Only electronic responses to the above email address will be accepted. DOE will not consider responses submitted by any other means. FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: DOECriticalMinerals@doe.gov

title: Environmental Science and Engineering Contract, A-E Services to be Ordered on Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity Schedule
description: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE HAS BEEN UPDATED, SEEKING SF330 SUBMITALS. THERE IS NO RFP PACKAGE TO DOWNLOAD. ALL INFORMATION NEEDED TO SUBMIT SF330 DOCUMENT IS CONTAINED HEREIN. SF 254S AND SF 255S WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED. NOTE: FAR PART 12 (COMMERCIAL) IS NOT APPLICABLE TO THIS PROCUREMENT. SUMMARY: The Naval Facilities Engineering and Expeditionary Warfare Center (NAVFAC EXWC), Port Hueneme, California is soliciting SF330s for a single-award, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Architect and Engineering (A-E) contract for various environmental restoration (ER) and other environmental projects. The A-E services required will include professional services to enable NAVFAC EXWC to support other NAVFAC commands, as well as other Department of War (DoW) and federal agencies. Market research was conducted in May 2026 and there were too few qualified small businesses to warrant consideration of a set-aside, therefore this acquisition is being issued under Full and Open Competition. The North American industry Classification System (NAICS) code is the procurement 541330, and the annual size standard is $25,500,000. NAVFAC EXWC anticipates the award of an IDIQ with base ordering period of sixty (60) months, and an extension of services period not to exceed six months. The maximum value of all task order placed under this contract will not exceed $150,000,000. Individual task orders under this contract may be firm fixed price (FFP) (Estimated 40%) or cost-plus-fixed fee (CPFF) (Estimated 60%). The minimum guarantee for the IDIQ contract is $10,000. Individual task orders are anticipated to range $5,000 to $6,000,000 per task order. The estimated award date is March 2027. PROJECT INFORMATION: Firms must be capable of performing work on a wide variety of projects in Environmental Restoration (ER) and other environmental topics, in a manner that complies with federal, state, and local regulations and laws, and within timeframes required. This work will support the A-E services that NAVFAC EXWC provides to support the environmental cleanup of sites managed by the Department of the Navy and other federal agencies. Although, the majority of the work is expected to be in the continental United States, project sites could be worldwide. Specific needs will be determined based upon project requirements and as described in each task order�s Performance Work Statement or Statement of Work. A-E services required under this contract include, but are not limited to: - Environmental program development and implementation. Particularly, the contractor will support development and implementation of the Navy�s environmental restoration (ER) program, comprising the Installation Restoration (IR) and Munitions Response (MR) Programs in terms of the associated science and engineering, regulations, and policy - Research, development, testing, and evaluation (RDT&E) of innovative environmental technologies, techniques, and solutions, particularly for environmental restoration. - Planning and pilot-testing innovative environmental technologies, techniques, investigations, and solutions to support full-scale design. - Services for associated environmental programs, including remedy resilience, impacts of elevated sea water levels and extreme weather events, active range sustainability, sustainable water resources management, environmental compliance, energy efficiency, and natural resources management. The services at ER sites may involve supporting NAVFAC EXWC in the preparation, expert review, or optimization of preliminary assessments, site inspections, remedial investigations, feasibility studies, engineering evaluation/analysis (EECA), proposed plans, records of decision (RODs), remedial designs, sampling and analysis plans (SAPs) or Quality Assurance Project Plans (QAPPs), and five-year reviews for customers in the Department of the Navy and other federal agencies. These services may include site characterization, laboratory studies, and pilot testing with the aim of helping NAVFAC EXWC and its customers develop cost-effective full-scale designs and solutions for environmental projects. An important component of the services also is technology transfer (T2) to and training of the Department of the Navy and other federal agency personnel (and their contractors), who are engaged in ER or other environmental programs. Other environmental project areas may include (but are not limited to) remedy resilience, coastal flooding from seawater and groundwater, and extreme weather events, active range sustainability, sustainable water resource management, environmental compliance, energy efficiency, and natural resource management. For on-site investigations, firms must provide personnel with current health and safety training, as required by the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) and adhere to all NAVFAC requirements for Health and Safety. Task orders will be issued with a project/site specific Scope of Work under the general scope of the contract. Typically, requests for proposals issued for individual task orders will include a general Scope of Work or a performance-based acquisition Performance Work Statement, location of work, character and extent of services required, technical requirements in addition to the requirements contained within Statement of Architect and Engineering Services (SAES). SELECTION CRITERIA: The selection criteria are listed below in descending order of importance. Items (1) thru (5) are primary criteria and (6) thru (7) are secondary criteria. Secondary criteria will only be used as 'tie-breakers' among technically equal firms. (1) Professional Qualifications: Professional Qualifications: The offeror shall provide no more than thirteen (13) resumes in Section E of the Standard Form (SF) 330. If more resumes are submitted than requested, then only the first thirteen will be considered. Providing less resumes is encouraged if provided personnel fulfill multiple roles. Experience that is not related to the work described in this solicitation should not be included. Resumes shall not be more than 2 pages each. Firms will be evaluated in terms of the general professional qualifications and technical competence in areas of work described in the "Project Information" section above. The evaluation of the resumes will consider education, training, registration, certifications, overall and relevant experience, and longevity with the firm. Projects that demonstrate successful optimization efforts that reduced project cost or time and added unique technical value, successful execution of projects where standards and methods for execution were not commonly accepted, or projects that had complex hydrogeological and regulatory site conditions will be given preference. Additionally, projects performed for the Navy or DoW as opposed to other federal agencies or other clients are preferred. Experience on the resumes should be within the last 8 years to be considered relevant. Resumes should be presented in the following three categories: Program Manager (PGM), Project Managers (PMs), and Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) in the technical areas listed above. The PGM and PMs should have a degree in engineering (environmental, civil, chemical, or related), or geological sciences, professional registrations in at least one state of the United States, and at least five (5) years of experience in managing programs or projects of similar size and complexity as expected in this contract. The states of registration and certification of relevant personnel must be included on each resume in Section E of SF 330. One PGM resume and two (2) PM resumes are required.The resumes will be rated more favorably when they demonstrate specialized experience and technical competence in the following areas: � Investigation and/or remediation of environmental media contaminated with emerging contaminants, particularly PFAS, especially projects executed for the Navy or DoW; � Inve

title: Denmark – Agricultural services – Udbud af græsningsaftale ved Holmegaard Mose, Næstved
description: Naturstyrelsen Storstrøm udbyder en græsningsaftale ved Holmegaard Mose, Næstved. Græsningsarealet udgør 20 -40 ha afhængigt af det leverede antal dyr. Græsningssæsonen løber i perioden 1. april til 30. september, begge dage inklusive. Udbuddet omfatter græsning med får på to hovedarealer samt to mindre delarealer. Formålet med afgræsningen er at fremme dannelsen af højmose samt bekæmpe uønskede arter, som tagrør, blåtop, japanpileurt samt dunbirk. Kontrakten indgås for 5 år med for én forlængelse på yderligere 5 år på uændrede vilkår. For yderligere oplysninger om græsningens omfang, beliggenhed og krav i øvrigt henvises til udbudsmaterialet.

title: Copie Accompagnement du maître d'ouvrage pour la gare de Marin-Epagnier
description:
Présentation du projet – Module 1 : Construction de la nouvelle gare de Marin-Epagnier

La gare de Marin-Epagnier, située sur la ligne Berne – Neuchâtel, nécessite d’importants travaux de rénovation. Les installations destinées au public ne répondent pas aux exigences de la loi sur l’égalité des personnes handicapées ni à la norme relative à la longueur utile des quais. Dans le cadre de ce projet, la gare doit être réaménagée pour devenir un pôle de transport conforme aux normes, avec deux quais extérieurs, une longueur utile de quais de 220 m et un nouveau passage souterrain pour piétons.


Étendue des prestations - Module 1

Le chef de projet général « Construction » est responsable de la conception technique de tous les travaux relatifs aux voies ferrées, aux routes et aux travaux de génie civil (y compris les systèmes de drainage, les ouvrages d'art et les structures porteuses).

Le mandat comprend les phases suivantes, conformément à l'art. 3.2 du Règlement SIA 103/2020 :

- Phase 31 : avant-projet

- Phase 32 : projet de construction (option)

- Phase 33 : procédure d’autorisation / projet soumis à l’enquête publique (option)

- Phase 41 : appel d’offres, comparaison des offres, proposition d’attribution (option)

- Phase 51 : projet d’exécution (option)

- Phase 52 : exécution (öBL facultatif) (option)

- Phase 53 : Mise en service, clôture (option)


Conformément aux articles 3.3 et 3.4 du Règlement SIA 103/2020, le soumissionnaire prend en charge les tâches relevant des domaines de la direction générale, de la conception technique et de la direction des travaux (option). La direction générale des travaux ne fait pas partie du mandat. La BLS se réserve le droit d’assurer elle-même la direction des travaux du projet.

Les prestations des services spécialisés et de leurs mandataires doivent être coordonnées dans le temps avec ses propres prestations spécialisées (programme de travail coordonné). Les heures d'honoraires pour les phases 32 à 53 ont été estimées par le maître d'ouvrage et ne peuvent être modifiées dans le cadre de l'appel d'offres. Elles feront l'objet d'une nouvelle estimation à la fin de l'avant-projet. À l'issue de l'avant-projet, le maître d'ouvrage se réserve le droit de modifier l'organisation du projet. (Option)


Présentation du projet – Module 2 : remplacement du poste d’aiguillage de Marin-Epagnier

Dans le cadre du projet de rénovation de la gare et de mise en conformité avec la LHand, le renouvellement du poste d’aiguillage est prévu à Marin-Epagnier. Compte tenu de l’augmentation du volume de manœuvres sur le site, une mise en service anticipée du nouveau poste d’aiguillage d’ici 2030 permettra d’améliorer la sécurité d’exploitation dès que possible. L’installation de signaux nains permettra de mieux sécuriser les manœuvres et d’améliorer considérablement le niveau de sécurité dans l’exploitation quotidienne.

title: One Photonic Wafer Probe Station and one Photonic Assembly Station
description: This tender concerns DTU Nano's planned procurement of a Photonic Assembly Station and a Photonic Wafer Probe Station. The tender is split into to two lots – one for each of the two stations. Tenderers may choose to bid on one or both lots, which will be evaluated and awarded individually. The assembly station is for connecting fibre array units (FAUs) to an optical chip. The type of connection will be edge coupling using waveguides loops for alignment but if necessary, the alignment can also be performed either using the light source on the chip (if it exists) or by using an external light source and connecting two FAUs, one on each side of the chip. Thus, the main purpose of the machine is to do assembly and fiber attachment of photonic chips. The system shall support research, prototyping, process development, pilot manufacturing, and low-volume production activities within DTU Nano's advanced fabrication facility. DTU has activities within Silicon Photonics (SiPh), Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs), Optical transceivers, Laser modules, Photodetectors, Fiber-optic assemblies, Co-packaged optics and Quantum photonic devices which we want to support in the best possible way. DTU therefore intends to purchase a reconfigurable, flexible, versatile machine. The purpose of the photonic wafer probe station is to characterise the quality of photonic integrated circuits (PICs). It should be possible to characterise both optical and electrical performance. For the optical characterisation, the main coupling in/out technique will be through grating couplers, but the equipment should be possible to be configured also for edge coupling to component facets in a grove on the wafer. In this case, different holders and fibres may be needed. The electrical characteristics are to be characterised both in DC as well as RF up to 40GHz using probe and/or probe cards. The system shall support research, development, process qualification, and routine characterization activities within DTU Nano's advanced fabrication facility.

title: Ombygning af Aabenraa genbrugsplads
description: Arwos driver i dag en genbrugsplads med genbrugsbutik i Aabenraa. Arwos ønsker at skabe en fremtidssikret genbrugsplads, hvor det er muligt at udfolde initiativerne i den kommunale affaldsplan for Aabenraa Kommune. Affaldsplanens initiativer er fokuseret på cirkulær økonomi med mere direkte genbrug, salg i egen butik og samarbejder omkring ressourcer og partnerskaber. Nærværende projekt er betegnet som ”Ombygning af Aabenraa genbrugsplads” (herefter benævnt ”Projektet”). Projektet består i at gentænke genbrugspladsens funktion, indretning og drift med henblik på at etablere en fremtidssikret genbrugsplads. Projektet realiseres som en totalentreprise, hvor den valgte totalentreprenør får ansvaret for såvel projektering som udførelse af den endelige løsning. Bygherre har ikke på forhånd fastlagt den endelige løsning eller den nærmere tilrettelæggelse af totalentreprisen. Udbuddet gennemføres som en konkurrencepræget dialog, jf. udbudslovens §§ 67-72 (Lovbekendtgørelse 2025-02-03 nr. 116). Dette indebærer, at alene prækvalificerede har ret til at deltage i dialogfasen og afgive eventuelt tilbud. Enhver økonomisk aktør kan ansøge om deltagelse i udbuddet, og Bygherre vurderer ansøgerens egnethed for den videre deltagelse i udbudsforretningen. Konkurrencepræget dialog giver mulighed for at føre dialog med indbudte dialogdeltagere i dialogfasen med henblik på at kunne indkredse den løsning, der bedst opfylder bygherres behov, hvorefter der overgås til en tilbudsfase, der indeholder den egentlige tilbudsafgivning på baggrund af den/de valgte løsning(er). Nærværende udbud er således inddelt i 3 faser. Først en prækvalifikationsfase, som efterfølges af en dialogfase, som efterfølges af en tilbudsfase. Tilbudsfasen indeholder udsendelse af det endelige udbudsmateriale til alle, der er prækvalificerede til dialogen. Den konkurrenceprægede dialog gennemføres derfor med henblik på at identificere og udvikle de løsninger, der bedst understøtter Projektets målsætninger inden for Projektets rammer. Det Beskrivende Dokument indeholder betingelser for og vejledning om ansøgning om prækvalifikation til deltagelse i dialogfasen og afgivelse af tilbud på ovennævnte udbud. Derudover beskriver dokumentet den opgave, som Arwos udbyder og ønsker løsninger på.

title: Germany – Ancillary works for pipelines and cables – Rohrleitungsbauarbeiten zum BV "Sanierung Lietzenburger Straße"
description: Die BEW Berliner Energie und Wärme GmbH beabsichtigt die Vergabe von Tief- und Rohrleitungsbauleistungen zur Sanierung und Kapazitätserweiterung einer Fernwärmetrasse in der Lietzenburger Straße in Berlin. Der zu sanierende Trassenabschnitt umfasst eine Länge von ca. 950 m zwischen Sächsischer Straße und Rankestraße einschließlich der zugehörigen Hausanschlüsse und Verteiltrassen. Im Abschnitt zwischen Knesebeckstraße und Fasanenstraße werden die Arbeiten gemeinsam mit der NBB Netzgesellschaft Berlin-Brandenburg durchgeführt. Hierzu ist die Sanierung und teilweise Umverlegung einer bestehenden Gasleitung DN 800 erforderlich, um die notwendige Baufreiheit für die Verstärkung der Fernwärmetrasse zu schaffen. Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung sind die Rohrleitungsbauleistungen der BEW Berliner Energie und Wärme GmbH (Auftraggeber 1 / Leistungsabschnitt 1 - Los 1) sowie der NBB Netzgesellschaft Berlin-Brandenburg (Auftraggeber 2 / Leistungsabschnitt 2 - Los 2). Der Leistungsumfang umfasst insbesondere: • Neuverlegung von Kunststoffmantelrohrtrassen (KMR) in verschiedenen Nennweiten bis DN 600, • Anpassung und Wiederherstellung von Hausanschlüssen, Verteiltrassen und Pumpenhausanbindungen sowie • Gasleitungsbauarbeiten der NBB mit Demontage und Neuverlegung einer DN 800-Stahlgasleitung in teilweise geänderter Trassenlage. Die Baumaßnahme wird in sieben Bauabschnitte unterteilt und umfasst insgesamt den Rückbau von rund 800 m bestehender Fernwärmetrasse sowie die Neuverlegung von rund 1.000 m Fernwärmeleitungen unterschiedlicher Dimensionen. Ergänzend werden mehrere Schachtbauwerke saniert, neu errichtet oder zurückgebaut sowie zahlreiche Systemübergänge und Netzanbindungen hergestellt. Besondere Anforderungen bestehen in der Aufrechterhaltung der Wärmeversorgung während der gesamten Bauzeit durch betriebsbereite oberirdische Leitungsprovisorien. Gleichzeitig sind die Verkehrsführung sowie die Erreichbarkeit für Anwohner, Gewerbetreibende, Fußgänger und Radfahrer sicherzustellen. Aufgrund zahlreicher paralleler Infrastrukturvorhaben im Projektumfeld ist eine enge Abstimmung mit Behörden, Versorgungsträgern und Projektbeteiligten erforderlich. Zur Minimierung der Beeinträchtigungen ist vorgesehen, mehrere Bauabschnitte zeitgleich auszuführen.

title: Denmark – Construction work – Ombygning af Aabenraa genbrugsplads
description: Arwos driver i dag en genbrugsplads med genbrugsbutik i Aabenraa. Arwos ønsker at skabe en fremtidssikret genbrugsplads, hvor det er muligt at udfolde initiativerne i den kommunale affaldsplan for Aabenraa Kommune. Affaldsplanens initiativer er fokuseret på cirkulær økonomi med mere direkte genbrug, salg i egen butik og samarbejder omkring ressourcer og partnerskaber. Nærværende projekt er betegnet som ”Ombygning af Aabenraa genbrugsplads” (herefter benævnt ”Projektet”). Projektet består i at gentænke genbrugspladsens funktion, indretning og drift med henblik på at etablere en fremtidssikret genbrugsplads. Projektet realiseres som en totalentreprise, hvor den valgte totalentreprenør får ansvaret for såvel projektering som udførelse af den endelige løsning. Bygherre har ikke på forhånd fastlagt den endelige løsning eller den nærmere tilrettelæggelse af totalentreprisen. Udbuddet gennemføres som en konkurrencepræget dialog, jf. udbudslovens §§ 67-72 (Lovbekendtgørelse 2025-02-03 nr. 116). Dette indebærer, at alene prækvalificerede har ret til at deltage i dialogfasen og afgive eventuelt tilbud. Enhver økonomisk aktør kan ansøge om deltagelse i udbuddet, og Bygherre vurderer ansøgerens egnethed for den videre deltagelse i udbudsforretningen. Konkurrencepræget dialog giver mulighed for at føre dialog med indbudte dialogdeltagere i dialogfasen med henblik på at kunne indkredse den løsning, der bedst opfylder bygherres behov, hvorefter der overgås til en tilbudsfase, der indeholder den egentlige tilbudsafgivning på baggrund af den/de valgte løsning(er). Nærværende udbud er således inddelt i 3 faser. Først en prækvalifikationsfase, som efterfølges af en dialogfase, som efterfølges af en tilbudsfase. Tilbudsfasen indeholder udsendelse af det endelige udbudsmateriale til alle, der er prækvalificerede til dialogen. Den konkurrenceprægede dialog gennemføres derfor med henblik på at identificere og udvikle de løsninger, der bedst understøtter Projektets målsætninger inden for Projektets rammer. Det Beskrivende Dokument indeholder betingelser for og vejledning om ansøgning om prækvalifikation til deltagelse i dialogfasen og afgivelse af tilbud på ovennævnte udbud. Derudover beskriver dokumentet den opgave, som Arwos udbyder og ønsker løsninger på.

title: Germany – Business and management consultancy services – Konzeption und Steuerung für den Transaktionsprozess zur Veräußerung des WDR-Geländes in Köln-Bocklemünd
description: Der WDR beabsichtigt, den nördlichen Teil seines rund 58 ha umfassenden Areals in Köln-Bocklemünd zu veräußern. Das Gelände erstreckt sich beiderseits des Freimersdorfer Weges, ist teilweise bebaut und wird derzeit teilweise durch den WDR sowie durch Dritte genutzt. Vor dem Hintergrund sinkender Eigennutzung soll der Standort perspektivisch aufgegeben werden. Die vollständige Freiziehung des Areals wird für den Zeitraum zwischen 2028 und 2035 erwartet. Eine Veräußerung kann grundsätzlich auch vor vollständiger Freiziehung erfolgen. Die zu vergebende Leistung umfasst die Konzeption und Steuerung des gesamten Transaktionsprozesses durch ein erfahrenes Beratungsunternehmen. Der Auftragnehmer unterstützt den WDR bei der Vorbereitung, Vermarktung, Durchführung und Begleitung der Investorenauswahl sowie bei der kaufmännischen Abwicklung des Verkaufsprozesses bis zur Auswahl eines bevorzugten Investors. Parallel zur vorliegenden Ausschreibung wird eine Beratung für ein separates Interessenbekundungsverfahren beauftragt. Das Interessenbekundungsverfahren wird somit durch einen gesonderten Auftragnehmer begleitet. Die Ergebnisse dieses Verfahrens sind durch den Auftragnehmer der Transaktionsberatung zu berücksichtigen und in den weiteren Transaktionsprozess einzubeziehen. Die rechtliche Beratung der Transaktion sowie die Vertragsgestaltung und -verhandlung erfolgen durch gesondert beauftragte Berater und sind nicht Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung. Hinweis: In der Teilnahmebroschüre und der Vergabeunterlagen sind grundsätzlich alle Informationen enthalten, die zur Beurteilung des Gesamtprojektes notwendig sind. Die im Teilnahmewettbewerb erfolgreichen Bewerber werden jedoch weitergehende Informationen erhalten, die aus Geheimhaltungsgründen nicht auf der Vergabeplattform veröffentlicht werden. Diese betreffen beispielsweise Auswertungen und bereits erfolgte Prüfungen hinsichtlich des Gesamtprojektes.

title: Germany – Land rental or sale services – Kartellrechtliches Auswahlverfahren zur Vergabe von Industrie- und Gewerbeflächen im Bereich des Voslapper Groden Nord
description: Der Containerterminal JadeWeserPort wurde offiziell am 21.09.2012 durch den Betreiber, die Eurogate CTW GmbH & Co KG, in Betrieb genommen. Neben dem Containerterminal ist das trimodale Güterverkehrszentrum JadeWeserPort (nachfolgend "GVZ JadeWeserPort") entstanden, welches von dem Eigentümer entwickelt und betrieben wird. Ergänzend hierzu hat JWP-M im Jahr 2026 das Eigentum an Flächen im Bereich des Voslapper Groden Nord (VGN) erworben. Die Flächen des VGN sollen als Energy Hub Cluster mit ggf. trimodaler Anbindung (Wasser-Bahn-Straße) weiterentwickelt und genutzt werden. Für einen Teil der derzeit noch nicht durch Vertragsschluss vergebenen Gewerbeflächen des Industriegebiets mit einer Größe von insgesamt ca. 400.000 m² (im Folgenden: Vermarktungsflächen) sollen mit diesem Auswahlverfahren Grundstücksverträge für Ansiedlungen aus dem Bereich der erneuerbaren Energien und/oder energieintensive Industrien vergeben werden. Hierzu sollen Grundstücksverträge geschlossen werden, die die jeweiligen Ansiedler verpflichten, den Standort möglichst hafenaffin (mit wasserseitigem Umschlag über die bei den Landesgesellschaften des Landes Niedersachsen vorhandenen und in Zukunft zu errichtenden Hafeninfrastrukturen) mit der Zweckbestimmung Industriegebiet für erneuerbare Energien und/oder energieintensive Industrien ("Energy Hub"; im Folgenden: Industriegebiet) dauerhaft zu betreiben. Die Grundstücksverträge werden entsprechende Verpflichtungen zum Bau und zur Inbetriebnahme/zum Betrieb der Betriebsgebäude/Produktionsstätten enthalten.

title: Germany – Business development consultancy services – Hochrangige Regierungsberatung in Osteuropa, auf dem Westbalkan, im Südkaukasus und in Zentralasien - Beratungsleistungen zur Unterstützung wirtschaftspolitischer Reformprozesse
description: Die hochrangige Regierungsberatung wird in Staaten in Osteuropa, auf dem Westbalkan, im Südkaukasus und in Zentralasien durchgeführt. Aktuell erfolgt die Beratung in den Ländern Ukraine, Belarus (derzeit ausgesetzt), Moldau, Georgien (derzeit ausgesetzt), Usbekistan und Kosovo. Ab 2027 soll die Beratung in den Ländern Ukraine, Moldau, Usbekistan, Kosovo, Albanien und Nordmazedonien erfolgen. Bei Bereitstellung zusätzlicher Haushaltsmittel ist als weiteres Programmland Armenien vorgesehen. Kern und Voraussetzung für die Akzeptanz der Beratung bei den Regierungen der Zielländer ist die Unabhängigkeit und Nachfrageorientierung der Beratung. Die Beratung wird auf Wunsch und Nachfrage von Institutionen des Partnerlandes erbracht. Die konkreten Themen für die wirtschaftspolitische Beratung werden vorrangig von Institutionen und Regierungsstellen der Partnerländer dem AN oder dem BMWE gegenüber vorgeschlagen. Damit ergänzt die Regierungsberatung das Instrumentarium der Außenwirtschaftsförderinstrumente, die sich vornehmlich an Unternehmen richten. Der AN tritt in der Ausführung des Auftrags als eigenständiger Akteur auf. Der AN hat in Abstimmung mit dem AG auf das Auftragsverhältnis zu verweisen.

title: Nedrivning og miljøsanering af Sankt Lukas Vej 7A-7C - Hovedentreprise
description: Gentofte Kommune udbyder som hovedentreprise nedrivning og miljøsanering af den eksisterende bebyggelse på Sankt Lukas Vej 7A-7C, matr.nr. 8li, Gentofte. Nedrivningen klargør grunden til opførelsen af Ny Lindely Plejehjem, som udbydes som totalentreprise i et selvstændigt udbud (TED 607791-2026). Grunden overdrages til totalentreprenøren ved afleveringen. Nedrivningen omfatter ca. 1.980 m² bygningsareal inkl. kælder fordelt på tre adresser, Sankt Lukas Vej 7A, 7B og 7C, samt tilhørende befæstede arealer, fundamenter, terrændæk, installationer og ledningsanlæg. Entreprisen omfatter miljøsanering forud for nedrivningen, herunder fjernelse og bortskaffelse af asbest, PCB, bly og øvrige miljøfarlige stoffer, samt selektiv nedrivning med sortering og genanvendelse af bygge- og anlægsaffald. De gule mursten fra bebyggelsen skal nedtages, afrenses, dokumenteres og opbevares i depot med henblik på genbrug i nybyggeriet. Det tilstødende plejehjem på Sankt Lukas Vej 9A er i fuld drift under hele nedrivningen, og der forventes sideløbende byggeaktivitet på nabomatriklen. Arbejdet skal udføres på en arealmæssigt begrænset byggeplads med delt adgangsvej, begrænsning af støj, støv og vibrationer og koordinering med naboprojektet. Udbuddet omfatter desuden optioner på en midlertidig alternativ vejadgang og nedrivning af en mellemgang mellem Lindely Plejecenter og Sankt Lukas Stiftelsens bygning.

title: Audience Research and Segmentation Studies in Eastern Europe and the Western Balkans
description: International Media Support (IMS) seeks to establish a pool of qualified research providers through framework agreements to deliver recurring audience segmentation studies and related audience intelligence services across Eastern Europe and the Western Balkans. IMS reserves the right to enter into more than one framework agreement as a result of this tender. Across the region, disinformation, information manipulation, and declining trust in information sources continue to affect public discourse and democratic resilience. To design effective responses, media organisations, civil society actors, and other stakeholders require a deeper understanding of audience behaviours, information needs, media consumption habits, levels of trust, and vulnerability to harmful narratives. Through this tender, IMS aims to identify service providers capable of designing and implementing audience segmentation studies and related research in multiple countries across Eastern Europe and the Western Balkans. The findings will support IMS and its partners in developing evidence-based strategies, content, engagement approaches, and interventions that strengthen information integrity and more effectively reach priority audiences. Applications are welcome from research companies, consultancies, academic institutions, and consortia with the required expertise and capacity to deliver high-quality audience research services across the target regions.
